title: Article 84 — Qualification for membership of Parliament

content.overview: Article 84 — Qualification for membership of Parliament. Complete constitutional treatise with procedural anchors, cases, and chamber drafting blueprints.
content.study:
Topic at a Glance
Article 84 of the Constitution of India is titled “Qualification for membership of Parliament”. It forms an integral component of The Union (Articles 52–151), located within the “The Union” cluster. Current through the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023.

Constitutional Text & Anatomy
A person shall not be qualified to be chosen to fill a seat in Parliament unless he— (a) is a citizen of India, and makes and subscribes before some person authorised in that behalf by the Election Commission an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in the Third Schedule;

(b) is, in the case of a seat in the Council of States, not less than thirty years of age and, in the case of a seat in the House of the People, not less than twenty-five years of age; and

(c) possesses such other qualifications as may be prescribed in that behalf by or under any law made by Parliament. . and further subs. by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 13, for \
